Title: A New Hat
Content: “How was school today?” Dad asked Ava when she got home.
“Good,” Ava said, “but my head was cold. I need a new hat that is warm and looks good.”
“Okay, let's see if we can find a hat that you can wear tomorrow,” Dad said. “Try my hat.”
Ava tried on Dad's wool cap. It was very warm, but it didn't look good. It was too big.
“Here, try on Mom's hat,” Dad said, handing a baseball cap to Ava.
The hat looked good on Ava's head, but it was not at all warm.
“You could try putting on Levi's hat,” Dad said, handing Ava her baby brother's tiny hat.
Levi's hat might have been warm and looked good, but Ava couldn't even get it on her head!
“Maybe we could make a new hat,” Ava suggested.
“We could make `text(one)` out of an old shirt,” Dad said.
“Dad, a shirt goes on your body, not on your head,” Ava said.
“I know that,” Dad said, smiling at Ava. “Let's see what we can do anyway.”

They found a warm fleece shirt that Ava had outgrown. Ava used to love that shirt. She used to wear it all the time. Ava was surprised and a little sad when Dad snipped off the bottom `text(half)` of the shirt. Then, he tied `text(one)` end in a knot.
Ava's new hat fit perfectly, it was warm, and it looked great!
